business_problem: MHCLG's high-rise building survey included nuanced free-text responses that needed to be structured and standardised for robust analysis and policy development.
solution_summary: GAD analysed MHCLG's high-rise-building survey, whose design included free-text responses alongside quantitative collection. The source does not name an intake connector, AI model or service, hosting environment, storage layer, or dashboard product. GAD used generative AI to transform the unstructured responses into structured data and standardise entries, making them suitable for more robust analysis. Working with MHCLG, GAD developed an interactive dashboard through which users can interrogate the results, drill into topics, compare geographic variation, and visualise change over time. The dashboard presents the analysis to decision-makers; actuaries, policy officials, economists, and delivery specialists collaborated on the work. The source reports that findings informed MHCLG's policy approach and evaluation of policy options and cost-effectiveness, but gives no technical detail about how processed data is persisted or how the dashboard is deployed.
data_flow: Free-text responses from MHCLG's high-rise building survey were transformed by AI into structured, standardised data for analysis. GAD and MHCLG presented the results in an interactive dashboard for users to explore topics, geographic variations, and change over time. The source does not describe storage or deployment.
business_outcome: The findings shaped MHCLG's policy approach and supported evaluation of policy options and their cost-effectiveness. The adoption of generative AI and data visualisation delivered significant efficiency savings and supported evidence-based decisions.
